QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Performance and Benchmarking_22

question.text: In the PDF's best-case scenario for Fund ABC (Category II AIF, 5-year life), Gross IRR is computed at 18.13% while Net IRR is 12.98%. What primarily drives this ~5 percentage point drag?

answer.text: Cumulative impact of initial set-up cost, yearly fund expenses, management fees (1.5% + GST), incentive fees and capital gains tax — all borne by investors indirectly.
Sub-optimal exit valuations on concentrated holdings.
The fund has over-committed capital to a single investee company exceeding 25%.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 7.3.1 'Conclusion': 'Net IRR can substantially be below the Gross IRR, if the fund has high fixed costs in terms of set-up costs, operating expenses, management fees and incentive fees.' The Best-case split 18.13% → 12.98% is ~515 bps drag driven by: set-up INR 1.25 cr amortised, yearly expenses INR 30 lakh, mgmt fee 1.5%+GST on Gross NAV, 15% incentive fee on INR 24.56 cr excess, and 10.4% LTCG tax. The Trap: A would cap Gross IRR — but here Gross IRR is the numerator already. C is a separate regulatory breach. D only affects foreign LPs, not domestic Net IRR. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C, XIX-A test identical mechanics. XXI-B PMS has a similar but smaller drag (no entry tax, typically no carry on listed PMS). Manager's Pro-Tip: Always show LPs a waterfall of 'Gross IRR → Net IRR' bridge with each line-item drag — LPs respect transparent fee/tax attribution far more than a single Net IRR number.
